text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Democratic Party leader Spyros Kyprianou scores a significant victory at party congress, changing an article of its constitution allowing him to run as candidate in presidential elections.
- President Glafcos Clerides expects European interest in the Cyprus problem to continue.
- Communications and works ministry has rejected application of Lumiere TV to transmit on an open circuit.
- The rift in the Democratic Party was made official. Party member Tasos Papadopoulos disagrees with change in constitution allowing party leaders to run for the presidency.
- The United States are pushing for a package deal to solve the Cyprus problem.
- Britain does not want any change in its status as a guarantor power of Cyprus's independence.
- Authorities dismiss suggestions telephone lines in Nicosia area are responsible for cancer reported among residents.
- Paphos residents complain to the president that foreigners have turned neighbourhoods into little ghettos.
- Kyprianou wins constitution debate at party conference.
- Chairman of the clothing manufacturers association confirms the Cypriot market is full of cheap designer clothes rip-offs.
- The Nikiforos military exercise enters its major phase today.
